visualizerParams.title: Code Refactor: OrderedDict Instead of a Dict plus an Order List
visualizerParams.problemDescription: A dictionary stores the values and a separate list tracks the order of use, which has to be kept in step by hand. Use one OrderedDict. The output must stay the same.
visualizerParams.initialCode:
data = {}
order = []


def use(key):
    if key in order:
        order.remove(key)
    order.append(key)


def put(key, value, capacity):
    data[key] = value
    use(key)
    if len(order) > capacity:
        oldest = order.pop(0)
        del data[oldest]


put("a", 1, 2)
put("b", 2, 2)
use("a")
put("c", 3, 2)
print(order)

solution.code:
from collections import OrderedDict

cache = OrderedDict()


def put(key, value, capacity):
    cache[key] = value
    cache.move_to_end(key)
    if len(cache) > capacity:
        cache.popitem(last=False)


put("a", 1, 2)
put("b", 2, 2)
cache.move_to_end("a")
put("c", 3, 2)
print(list(cache))
solution.explanation: One structure holds both the values and their order, so the two can never get out of step, and move_to_end and popitem do the list juggling.
